question: Can any strategy be scored on money, not just on probabilities?
what_we_know: No. The repository holds no licensed price for any market. Every ROI, CLV and 'edge' claim is therefore uncomputable, and the comparison lab scores proper scores and pricing error only. There is a third-party reference-quote file in the repo, but it is not licensed, not timestamped at open/close, and not an official NFL source.
what_we_do_not_know: Whether a price feed will be licensed at all; the price-data policy (which book, which snapshot time, open/close definition, void/push rules); how the model and market keys join.
blocks: Every money-denominated leaderboard, every reward tier, the parlay gate (R058) and the vig decomposition (R049).
would_clear_it: One written price-data policy committed before any backtest, plus a retained feed with open and close quotes per market and a settlement key. Then R051's comparison can gain an ROI column without changing anything else.

question: Is any strategy's side signal distinguishable from luck?
what_we_know: Four strategies beat the coin on Brier score over 132 walk-forward games: skill +5.95% (S1), +6.28% (S2), +7.59% (S3), +6.54% (S4). All four also beat a pick'em margin on MAE (10.03 to 10.38 vs 10.66). But the best of the four, S2, reaches only z = -2.43 on margin gain (z = -2.11 on Brier), against a Bonferroni critical value of 2.87 for 12 comparisons. Nothing survives.
what_we_do_not_know: Whether a bigger sample keeps the sign; whether the ordering of the four arms is stable; whether the effect is big enough to clear a real bookmaker's margin, which is around 4.5% of the two-way price and larger than the 6-8% Brier improvement suggests.
blocks: Any claim of skill, any promotion of a strategy, any live deployment.
would_clear_it: About 700-900 walk-forward games (roughly three seasons) for the current effect size to clear a Bonferroni-adjusted threshold at 80% power. That is an arithmetic requirement, not an opinion: the interval has to shrink by about a factor of three.

question: Why are the totals not working, and is that fixable?
what_we_know: The model's predicted total has essentially no relationship with the actual total: r = -0.03, 95% interval [-0.22, +0.17], n = 148. Worse, a control that ignores both clubs entirely (the trailing league mean) beats every strategy on total MAE: 11.36 vs 11.55-11.56.
what_we_do_not_know: Whether total signal exists in inputs this repo does not hold: pace with situation (score, clock), offensive line health, weather, roof, referee crew, and the market's own total as an anchor.
blocks: The totals leg of every originated line, any totals-based strategy, and any same-game parlay that combines a side with a total.
would_clear_it: Either a demonstrable gain over the trailing-mean control on a walk-forward window, or an explicit decision to originate totals as 'league mean plus nothing' and label them that way.

question: Is the model too timid to beat a price even when it is right?
what_we_know: No - the opposite. The dispersion ratio (SD of predicted margin divided by SD of actual margin) is 0.26 for S2, 0.44 for S4, 0.51 for S1 and 0.58 for S3. The model's opinions are between a quarter and a half as spread out as reality. A shrink-to-the-mean rating will always produce this, and no average accuracy can compensate: the model will agree with the market almost everywhere and never have a large enough disagreement to cover the vig.
what_we_do_not_know: Whether widening the spread is calibration or overfitting; which shrinkage constant is honest; whether any widening survives out of sample.
blocks: Any claim of an edge over a market line. Under-dispersion is the mechanical reason the repo cannot produce a bettable number yet.
would_clear_it: Re-fit the shrinkage with a walk-forward objective (minimise Brier, not MAE) and publish the dispersion ratio beside every line. The ratio, not the MAE, is the number that predicts whether a line is bettable.

question: Does home field move the total, or only the margin?
what_we_know: Unknown, and it matters: the three total estimators tested (pace, offence-only, pace-plus-home-field) are within 0.28 points of each other on MAE across 132 games, with all paired differences at |z| < 0.95. Week 11's forecast for IND-HOU still carries a 2.4-point gap between the pace and offence-only estimators because there is no evidence to choose.
what_we_do_not_know: The size and sign of the home-field effect on the total in this league, this season, with this rule set.
blocks: Which total to publish. R051 requires two estimators to stay visible until one wins; this is that rule doing its job.
would_clear_it: A walk-forward comparison on a sample about four times larger, or an external published estimate that this repo is allowed to cite as an input rather than a fact.

question: Does the repo have a point-in-time record that a backtest can legally use?
what_we_know: Partly. There are two dated transcriptions of the Week 10 injury report (2026-11-14 and 2026-11-16) and a scheduled capture workflow, but both Week 10 reads were taken after those games were played, so neither is a pre-kickoff record. The scheduled workflow has never stored a capture: run 43974503837 (2026-11-16T22:54Z) failed with exit code 2, which is its drift alarm firing because the Week 11 route still served the final Week 10 tables. That was a defect in the alarm, not in the page, and it has been fixed in this session: not-published-yet is now recorded distinctly from drift and is unit-tested.
what_we_do_not_know: Whether the scheduled capture works at all against the live page; whether a full Wednesday-to-kickoff series exists for any week; whether the fixture-venue and weather fields can be captured on the same clock.
blocks: Every availability feature, the depth-deficiency matrix, and any claim that a forecast was made before kickoff using only what was known then.
would_clear_it: One complete week of scheduled captures (Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday morning) with retained hashes, verified by a re-run that reproduces the same rows. Fix the failing workflow first.

question: Is Week 11 data available yet, and what does that mean for a prospective test?
what_we_know: No. As of 2026-11-17 the official injury report for Week 11 is not published: nfl.com/injuries/league/2026/reg11 still serves the Week 10 tables (final), and the game-centre pages for Week 11 fixtures report 'Injury Report is not available at this time'. The Week 11 schedule is published: 13 games, 6 clubs on bye, one international game (MIN at SF, Mexico City) and one neutral-site note to verify.
what_we_do_not_know: When the Week 11 report appears (the league's own cadence implies Wednesday); whether any Week 11 fixture moves under flex scheduling.
blocks: The first genuinely prospective origination. The Week 11 slate is published on this page with every market column blank rather than guessed.
would_clear_it: Capture the Week 11 report the day it appears, with a hash and a fetch time, then re-score these forecasts after the games. The forecasts on this page are the registration.

question: Can the 136-game log actually serve as the pre-registered backtest corpus?
what_we_know: Yes, and it reconciles exactly. The 148-game verified corpus contains precisely 136 games from weeks 1-9 (6,246 points), which is the brief's '136-game log'. Add the one Thursday Week 10 final (WAS 24-21 NYG) and you get the board's 137-game snapshot at 6,291 points; add the other 11 Week 10 finals and you get 148 games at 6,824 points. Every step's points change by exactly the points scored in the games added, and all 32 clubs' W/L/T/PF/PA match the official standings on both snapshots. Both counts in the repo were right; they were read at different clock times.
what_we_do_not_know: Nothing about the counts. What is still missing is the rest of the season: 148 games is weeks 1-10 of an 18-week schedule, and the evaluation needs multiple seasons, not a bigger slice of one.
blocks: Nothing. This question was the one blocking item that turned out to be already satisfied; it is kept here because the reconciliation is the proof and the proof belongs in the register.
would_clear_it: Cleared on 2026-11-17 by scripts/build_crosscheck.py, which reproduces the chain 136 -> 137 -> 148 and verifies both standings snapshots club by club. Re-runnable with --check.

question: Can '2nd/3rd/4th string' be established from an official source?
what_we_know: No. NFL.com publishes player rows without a depth ordinal, and the club charts are only partly accessible; the repo's depth order is a declared third-party transcription for 14 clubs plus a partial transcription for the rest. The official report gives a designation, not a rank.
what_we_do_not_know: Whether any official NFL source publishes a numeric depth order, or snap counts that could stand in as a proxy.
blocks: The matchup matrix, the backup-deficiency feature, and any claim that a named player is a club's second-string.
would_clear_it: Either a verified club-chart route for all 32 clubs, or an official snap-count source, before the feature is built (this is R042, and it is a gate, not a preference).

question: Does an injury designation tell us anything actionable?
what_we_know: Not yet measured here. The Week 10 report carries 347 listed rows of which only a fraction carry a game designation; 'Questionable' has no published percentage, and no inactive list has been captured, so the play rate per designation cannot be computed from this repo. Nothing on this page treats a designation as a probability.
what_we_do_not_know: The empirical play rate of Questionable, Doubtful and practice-status combinations, with intervals, on this season's rules.
blocks: Any injury term in the model, including the fixed penalty weights still present elsewhere in the repo.
would_clear_it: Join several seasons of designations to official inactive lists (R043). Until then, availability enters the model as an ablation, not as a penalty - which is exactly what the brief asks for.

question: What exactly must happen before a strategy may be declared the winner of this leaderboard?
what_we_know: A written sequence, published here: (1) pre-register the rule text and the sample window as a commit; (2) qualify on a proper score against a named control with a game-cluster interval; (3) survive a multiplicity adjustment for the number of arms actually tried; (4) hold the sign on a disjoint regime; (5) clear a price-based test with a licensed quote, which is impossible today. No strategy on this page has passed (3).
what_we_do_not_know: Who signs off; how many arms count as 'tried' (this page declares 12 and publishes the adjusted threshold); what happens to a strategy that fails after passing.
blocks: Any promotion, any demotion gate, any reward.
would_clear_it: A pre-registered competition document that names the arms in advance, so the multiplicity count is fixed before results are seen rather than after.

question: How is the reward assigned, and to what?
what_we_know: Undefined. There is no reward mechanism in the repo that is not design-only, and the two candidate bases - realised ROI and proper-score skill - disagree by construction. This page separates them: every strategy has a skill number and a staking number, and the staking number is empty because no price exists.
what_we_do_not_know: The scoring currency (skill or money), the payout rule, and whether the reward is reputational or financial.
would_clear_it: Pick the currency first. If the answer is money, QO-01 must be resolved first; if the answer is skill, publish the pre-registered threshold and the sample size before the season, not after.

question: Which single number tells us whether a backtest is even worth running?
what_we_know: The dispersion ratio and the interval width. On this page the four strategies differ from each other by less than their own intervals, and every interval is about 2.5-3 points of MAE wide on 132 games. A backtest on 148 games can therefore confirm that a model is reasonable and can never establish that it is better than another reasonable model.
what_we_do_not_know: How many games are needed for the current effect size - the arithmetic answer is roughly 700-900, i.e. multiple seasons.
would_clear_it: Publish the required sample size next to every ranking column, and refuse to rank until it is reached.

question: Are our own published pages consistent with the values we now compute?
what_we_know: Not entirely, and the differences are published rather than smoothed: the root site's Week 10 line page predates the final scores, the board's line series and this lab's recomputation disagree by a few tenths on some fixtures, and the earlier '11-game' evaluation used a different exclusion rule. Each figure on this page states its own n and window.
what_we_do_not_know: Which series is canonical (R070 is still NOT STARTED).
blocks: A single 'our line' number for any fixture.
would_clear_it: Choose one canonical series by commit hash, publish a deprecation notice on the others, and never compare across series silently.

question: Do the correlations on this page support any parlay at all?
what_we_know: No. Margin and total in the same game correlate at r = -0.15 (95% interval [-0.30, -0.01], n = 148): mildly negative, not independent, and the interval nearly touches zero. Multiplying two marginal probabilities would be wrong in a direction this sample cannot pin down. The repo publishes this number with its n; it does not publish a parlay.
what_we_do_not_know: A directly validated joint probability, the operator's void/push rules, and a correlation estimate stable across seasons.
blocks: Every parlay, same-game parlay and prop-combo strategy (R058).
would_clear_it: A joint model of (margin, total) validated on the same walk-forward window, plus the operator's rules in writing.
